Handler for Oceandata data sets

Source: R/oceandata.R
bb_handler_oceandata.Rd

This is a handler function to be used with data sets from NASA's Oceandata system. This function is not intended to be called directly, but rather is specified as a method option in bb_source.

bb_handler_oceandata(
  search,
  sensor,
  dtype,
  dtid,
  period,
  resolution_id,
  prod_id,
  suite_id,
  sdate,
  edate,
  ...
)

Arguments

search

character: the search string (file name pattern). Note that relying on the search string tends to yield slower searches: specify the target files as tightly as possible using the other search parameters. But you might still need the search string to impose additional filtering on the results

sensor

character: the sensor, e.g. "SeaWiFS", "MODISA", "MODIST", "VIIRS", "CZCS", "MERIS", etc: see https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/

dtype

character: the data type (e.g. "L3m") to pass to the oceancolor file searcher. Valid options at the time of writing are L0, L1, L2, L3b (for binned data), L3m (for mapped data), MET (for ancillary data), misc (for sundry products)

dtid

integer: data type ID, see https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/. Note that providing the dtid typically gives a much faster search

period

character: the time period, one of "DAY", (daily) "8D" (8-day), "MO", (monthly) "MC" (monthly climatology), "YR" (yearly), "SN" (seasonal), "SC" (seasonal climatology), etc: see https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/

resolution_id

character: "9km" or "4km"

prod_id

character: product, e.g. "par", "chlor_a", etc: see https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/

suite_id

character: product suite, e.g. "RRS", etc: see https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/

sdate

Date or character: start date (in "YYYY-MM-DD" format, if provided as a string)

edate

Date or character: end date (in "YYYY-MM-DD" format, if provided as a string). If not specified it will default to the current date

...

: extra parameters passed automatically by bb_sync

Value

TRUE on success

Details

Note that users will need an Earthdata login, see https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/. Users will also need to authorize the application 'OB.DAAC Data Access' (see 'My Applications' at https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/profile). Dry runs (listing files but not downloading them) can be performed without authentication.

Previously it was possible to search based on filename pattern alone, e.g. "S*L3m_MO_CHL_chlor_a_9km.nc" would match monthly level-3 mapped chlorophyll data from the SeaWiFS satellite at 9km resolution, in netcdf format. However, as of June 2026 the OB.DAAC search API requires other parameters to be set, in order to reduce the search load on the server, see https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/alerts-outages/ob.daac-file-search-utility-now-requires-more-specificity. It is not obvious which or how many parameters are required for a given search. If you are constructing an oceandata bowerbird source you are advised to use the file search web page https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/api/file_search and its help page https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/ to help find the correct parameters.

It is possible to provide multiple values for one or more search parameters: the POST request to the file search API will be repeated for all possible combinations of parameters (constructed via expand.grid). This might be helpful, for example, by allowing dtid to be specified as a two-element vector with one value for refined data and the second for NRT data. Specifying two dtid values will yield a much faster search than omitting dtid and relying on the search parameter to achieve the same refined/NRT file inclusions.

Note that the bb_handler_oceandata does not take need `source_url` to be specified in the bb_source call.

References

https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/, https://oceandata.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/file_search/file_search_help/, https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/alerts-outages/ob.daac-file-search-utility-now-requires-more-specificity

Examples


my_source <- bb_source(
  name = "Oceandata SeaWiFS Level-3 mapped monthly 9km chl-a",
  id = "SeaWiFS_L3m_MO_CHL_chlor_a_9km",
  description = "Monthly remote-sensing chlorophyll-a from the SeaWiFS satellite at
    9km spatial resolution",
  doc_url = "https://oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/",
  citation = "See https://oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/citations",
  license = "Please cite",
  method = list("bb_handler_oceandata", sensor = "SeaWiFS", dtype = "L3m",
                dtid = 1123, period = "MO", resolution_id = "9km", prod_id = "chlor_a",
                sdate = "1997-09-01", edate = "2011-01-01"),
  postprocess = NULL,
  collection_size = 7.2,
  user = "USERNAME", password = "PASSWORD",
  data_group = "Ocean colour")
